title: Apple Redistribution into Boxes
summary: Given an array of apple counts and an array of box capacities, determine the least number of boxes required to redistribute all apples from packs into boxes, allowing apples from the same pack to be placed in different boxes.
statement: Given an array of apple counts and an array of box capacities, determine the least number of boxes required to redistribute all apples from packs into boxes, allowing apples from the same pack to be placed in different boxes.
constraints: All apples may be redistributed among available boxes.
Choose the fewest boxes whose combined capacity holds the total number of apples.
The input guarantees total capacity is sufficient.
hints: Only total apple count matters because redistribution is unrestricted.
Sort box capacities from largest to smallest.
Accumulate them until their sum reaches the apple total.
For any fixed number of boxes, the largest capacities maximize available space, so the first sufficient prefix uses the fewest boxes.
editorial: For any fixed number of boxes, the largest capacities maximize available space, so the first sufficient prefix uses the fewest boxes.

tests.explanation: Six apples fit in the capacities five and four, so two boxes suffice.
All four boxes are needed to reach capacity fifteen.
